399.notes: Without a doubt, one of the better ending themes in the series, and definitely one of the best that isn't just a straight remix of the title theme; I do wish the initial theme was lingered on slightly more, but as is this is still a phenomenal track.

405.notes: Not a bad introduction to the series at all, but outside of the main melody lacks a secure sense of direction.

406.notes: Melancholic and a bit mournful, but also reverent. The second main section is honestly a bit too loud for me, I wish it had stayed quieter and more mournful the whole time; however, the melody in the third section is still quite beautiful, and the background instruments don't clutter it too much at all.

407.notes: Energetic and fun, but as-is, a bit cluttered; also suffers from being too short.

408.notes: Suffers a little bit from the base being samey, but the melodies are solid; could use being put over a less energetic bass.

409.notes: I feel cheated by that buildup not culminating in a big drop.

410.notes: A lot of good components here, but it's all a bit too in-your-face; the background instruments clutter the main melody a bit much, requiring it to have to try to stand out.

411.notes: Though the title seems to refer to such, this doesn't seem nearly energetic enough to be a Marisa theme.

412.notes: A strong melody, that isn't cluttered too much by the background, and a background that isn't too boring.

413.notes: The chorus on this is absolutely wonderful; would have scored much higher if not for the intro taking a long time to get going, and/or the chorus having other things happening withing its evolution, but thankfully the intro at least isn't bad.

414.notes: The chorus here isn't quite as good as in "Magic Mirror," but the parts outside of the chorus are all just about as good as it; the intro is haunting, and the bridge sections have clear, easy-to-follow melodies. The drums are a little intense, but not awful.

415.en_name: Now, Until the Moment You Die
415.notes: A classic for a reason, however there are parts of it that feel almost... empty? The intro is easily the most memorable part, and it runs out of interesting material after the first verse; it's also quite short, so I can't really justify rating it any higher.

416.notes: This track just screams triumph, with a clear melody that rings out throughout the beginning, leading into a mostly harmonic section with what are clearly designed after pizzicato string hits; I can just imagin that intro ringing out on french horrns and trombones, shaking you to your bones. The second verse is only slightly weaker, but leads very nicely back into the intro chorus.

417.notes: Suffers less from the feeling of emptiness than "Now, Until the Moment You Die" does in the beginning, but the second half is sadly just wholly less memorable. The ending is almost enough to push it over into an A.

418.notes: It's fine for an ending track, however the contrast between the background and the main melody is a little too much for me, and kinda hurts my ears.

915.jp_work: Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost
915.notes: This track sounds... heroic. Carrying one of my favorite melody lines in any recent Touhou game, and mixed beautifully, this track conveys all the mettle and majesty of someone strong and smart enough to become a villain to some in order to bcome a hero for all. Mix that with the mild creep factor present in many of the Animal Realm's tracks, and we have one of my favorite tracks in Touhou.
